title.narrative: GLA 2 - Uganda

description.narrative: Uganda’s country program will be delivered through 3 pathways; Pathway A on Indigenous Peoples andLocal Communities (which seeks to protect them against large developments and build their capacityto question and demand for their rights), Pathway B on Drivers of deforestation and forest degradation(that seeks to halt exploitation, infrastructure development and expansion of agro-commodities that are considered main drivers of deforestation and forest degradation) and Pathway C on Civic Spaces (that seeks to use environment and human rights defenders to open engagement spaces for positive engagement).The specific problems that will be addressed by the program include:Challenges to indigenous communities resulting from (a) the lack of power and opportunities to govern andmanage their landscape, limited involvement in decision making processes and (b) emerging pressure on their land and forests through external drivers.

comment.narrative: At the beginning of the GLA2 programme no laws have been blocked, adopted, improved for sustainable and inclusive development as a result of CSO engagement

2 laws were blocked, adopted, improved for sustainable and inclusive development as a result of CSO engagement at midline. For example, in June 2022 in Kampala, the president of Uganda, Yoweri Kaguta Museveni, signed the Electricity (Amendment) Bill, 2022 into law. The law is aimed at increasing Ugandan citizens’ access to affordable, reliable and clean energy. This should reduce pressure on Uganda’s forest landscapes.

The target of the GLA2 programme is to block, adopt or improve 2 laws for sustainable and inclusive development as a result of CSO engagement, specifically focusing on the oil and gas, agriculture and forestry sectors.
